topic: How Did Humans Get Their First Job?
title: The First Team Job
hook_promise: Why did we stop just hunting?

storylines.title: The Scavenger's Dilemma
storylines.hook: Why did we stop just hunting?
storylines.pitch: Early humans relied on big game, but aggressive scavenging only gave us 20% of the carcass. The stakes rose when mothers needed to forage while keeping infants safe.
storylines.conflict: A single hunter cannot secure enough food or protect a baby alone against predators and scarcity.
storylines.stakes: Starvation for the group if one person fails; death for the infant without protection.
storylines.twist: The solution wasn't better weapons, but trusted others holding infants while mothers worked—a shift from lone hunting to cooperative breeding.
storylines.payoff: This cooperation secured more food and saved lives, marking our first 'job' as a team player.
visuals: Host stands in front of a painted savanna scene with snow falling lightly.
Close-up on the host holding two sticks representing an infant and pointing to them being held by another stick figure.
Split screen: left shows one hunter struggling (myth), right shows cooperative group hunting (fact).
Camera moves from a wide shot of hunters to a close-up of hands passing food.

storylines.title: Three Reasons We Worked Together
storylines.pitch: Counting down the reasons humans got their first job: three to protect, two to survive, one to thrive forever.
storylines.conflict: Hunting alone is dangerous and inefficient; resources are scarce after the Ice Age ends.
storylines.stakes: Without a system, infants die in foraging trips and food goes to waste on carcasses we can't carry all of.
storylines.twist: Number one isn't just sharing meat, but cooperative breeding where others hold babies so mothers can hunt or gather safely.
storylines.payoff: This division of labor created the first stable human job: a caregiver and hunter working as a unit.
visuals: Host stands center stage holding up three painted stones for 'reason 3'.
Painted map with pins dropping to show hunting grounds shrinking over time (7950-3950 BCE).
Close-up of host swapping a stone for an infant stick figure held by another hand.
Host shrinks slightly in the frame as they explain 'reason 1', emphasizing intimacy and trust.

storylines.title: The Missing Hunter
storylines.pitch: In 7950 BCE, we find a mother foraging but no hunter nearby. The puzzle is how she survived without her partner.
storylines.conflict: A lone mother cannot safely gather food in dangerous terrain while carrying an infant alone.
storylines.stakes: The baby faces immediate danger from predators or the elements if left unattended during long trips.
storylines.twist: We discover a 'trusted other' holding the child, revealing that our first jobs were defined by social trust before money existed.
storylines.payoff: This mystery solves itself: humans got their first job through cooperative breeding networks, not just hunting skills.
visuals: Host stands in front of a painted forest scene with a question mark drawn above the host's head.
Camera zooms into a detail on the ground showing footprints leading away from a central camp.
Split screen: top shows a lone mother (myth), bottom reveals another figure holding an infant stick figure (fact).
Host holds up two sticks representing 'mother' and 'guardian' connecting them with string.

sources.claim: After the last Ice Age ended around 8000 BCE, early humans in this area were likely large game hunters.
sources.title: Earliest Humans - Curecanti National Recreation Area (U.S. National Park Service)
sources.quote: Native American presence in this area began as early as the Paleo-Indians around 8000 BCE (10,000 years ago). After the last Ice Age, the earliest people were likely large game hunters.

sources.claim: During the Early to Middle Archaic Period from roughly 7950 to 3950 BCE, humans lived a lifestyle defined by hunting and gathering.
sources.title: Earliest Humans - Curecanti National Recreation Area (U.S. National Park Service)
sources.quote: The most extensive occupation of Curecanti took place during the Early to Middle Archaic Period, approximately 7,950 to 3,950 BCE. This period is defined by hunting and gathering lifestyle and seasonal migrations.

sources.claim: Early humans acquired about 20% of big game carcasses through aggressive scavenging.
sources.title: Hunter-gatherer studies and human evolution: a very selective review
sources.quote: Of the big carcasses taken by people we were with, 20% were acquired by aggressive scavenging.

sources.claim: Cooperative breeding allowed mothers to forage while trusted others held their infants safely.
sources.title: Hunter-gatherer studies and human evolution: a very selective review
sources.quote: when social relationships assure the infant will be safely returned, mothers can net fitness benefits by foraging unencumbered while trusted others hold their infant
